sonnet.problem: The statement bundles two claims (Sihon comes out at Jahaz, and Sihon and his sons get away). The 'get away' part is also not clearly false from the text, which only says 'we defeated him and his sons and his whole army' and never says they were killed.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim.

sonnet.problem: The junk-drawer joke (stuck behind a takeout menu for a week) has no matching core action with the LORD giving Israel every city. It reads as a non sequitur and lands right after the heavy card about the cities' destruction.
sonnet.rule: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

sonnet.problem: It asks again whether the enemy army is delivered and some get away. Deuteronomy 3:3 repeats 2:33, and stop 1 card 15 already asked this same point with the same 'but they get away' shape.
sonnet.rule: When a line repeats in the passage, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears in this passage.

sonnet.problem: It asks about carrying off the livestock and plunder, which repeats Deuteronomy 2:35. Stop 1 card 17 already asked this and showed the answer, so it is asked a second time here.
sonnet.rule: When a line repeats in the passage, like a psalm's refrain, ask about it only the first time it appears in this passage.
